Abstract Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) integrates goal-directed decision-making, state continuity, planning, tool-mediated action, and feedback-driven adaptation into interactive computational systems. Although existing surveys examine agent capabilities, architectures, and applications, cross-paradigm comparisons often conflate functional capabilities with implementation mechanisms and organizational structures. This comprehensive narrative survey synthesizes foundational and contemporary research on symbolic/classical, neural/generative, neuro-symbolic, and multi-agent approaches to clarify conceptual boundaries and examine how agentic capabilities are architecturally realized. It organizes recurring functions into nine groups: goal and context management, perception and state representation, reasoning and decision-making, planning and replanning, memory and knowledge, action and tool use, evaluation and reflection, learning and adaptation, and coordination and orchestration. The principal contribution is an architecture-capability mapping separating functional responsibilities from computational mechanisms and coordination structures. A complementary conceptual reference architecture integrates goal management, environmental interaction, planning, memory, execution, evaluation, and cross-cutting assurance concerns. Representative cases demonstrate how different systems can realize similar functions using different mechanisms. The proposed taxonomy, formal abstraction, and reference architecture are analytical synthesis artifacts rather than experimentally validated models. They support transparent architectural comparison and identify testable research questions.

Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agentic workflows: systems in which an LLM plans tasks, retains memory, uses external tools, and coordinates with other agents to complete multi-step objectives. Existing surveys typically evaluate these components in isolation or rely on flat, mutually exclusive categorizations that conflate coordination patterns with functional roles and tooling. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review synthesizes 126 Scopus-indexed, peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2023 and June 2026, with screening conducted by a single reviewer. Because 122 of these articles appeared in 2025 and 2026, the corpus provides a timely, peer-evaluated evidence base for this rapidly accelerating field. Across seven research questions, we introduce a multi-layered taxonomy whose explicit novelty lies in strictly decoupling three primary coordination topologies (single-agent, collaborative multi-agent, and hierarchical supervisory) from orthogonal functional dimensions (role specialization), cross-cutting capability layers (tool augmentation and hybrid memory), and governance mechanisms (human-in-the-loop). Unlike prior rigid taxonomies that force systems into a single category, this structural separation systematically models modern hybrid implementations by combining distinct operational layers without artificial pigeonholing. Among the 57 empirical studies, collaborative multi-agent organization was the most frequently observed identifiable primary topology (27 studies, representing 47.4% of the empirical subset [ n = 27/57] and 21.4% of the total 126-study corpus). Across software engineering, healthcare, cybersecurity, and robotics, most reported implementations remain controlled research prototypes. Practical autonomy continues to be constrained by pipeline-level vulnerabilities: compounding error propagation, indirect prompt injection, memory poisoning, and the lack of standardized trajectory-level benchmarks. To advance agentic workflows toward dependable deployment, future research must prioritize standardized long-horizon evaluation, capability-based security architectures, and controlled self-evolution.

Abstract Background The world is facing a severe drug crisis, posing serious public health and societal risks. Yet, little is known about drug use among farmers and farmworkers, despite their essential role in global food production. This knowledge gap is particularly concerning because poor mental health and precarious working conditions are common in agriculture and may be associated with drug use as a coping mechanism, a relationship observed in other settings. However, evidence from agriculture remains extremely limited, largely due to data gaps. One challenge in collecting such data is social desirability bias, stemming from the topic’s sensitivity. We address this gap by using sensitive question techniques and provide novel evidence on drug use among farmers and farmworkers and its association with working conditions and work-related health. Methods We conducted item-count and item-sum double list experiments with 1,554 farmers and hired farmworkers between July and August 2023 to measure the prevalence and frequency of non-medical drug use in Nigeria’s labour-intensive tomato sector. Substances included cannabis, opioid painkillers such as tramadol and codeine, cough syrups, and similar drugs. List experiments avoid direct questioning and can estimate sensitive behaviours while hiding respondents’ answers from the interviewer. Using these estimates, we ran multivariate regressions on residualised outcome variables to identify work-related risk factors associated with drug use, focusing on burnout, work-related pain and health problems, pesticide exposure, unusual working hours, and belief in work performance effects. Results The item-count experiment suggests that about 8% of farmers, 20% of seasonal workers, and 6% of casual workers used drugs in the previous 12 months. The item-sum experiment estimates that drug-using farmers and seasonal workers consumed drugs on average about 8 days in the previous month, compared with about 7 days among drug-using casual workers. Multivariate regression analyses show that work-related pain and belief in performance-enhancing effects are the most important risk factors for frequent drug use. Our results also demonstrate that burnout levels are significantly higher among farmworkers than among farmers, but we do not find a significant association between work-related burnout and drug use. Conclusions Farmers and farmworkers suffer from important occupational health deficits. Drug use and mental health in rural areas in particular remain underappreciated on policy and research agendas. Implications for agricultural productivity and rural development should be further explored.

The article considers the possibility of introducing digital employees in the form of AI agents in the tourism sector. The author considers the features of AI agents as a new technology, summarizes and highlights seven key problems of implementing AI agents and provides a description of a typical AI agent architecture. The promising roles of AI agents in the tourism sector are highlighted separately and five potential areas of their application are described. Special emphasis is placed on the need to review the current business processes of travel companies in favor of adapting to the digital capabilities of AI agents as a promising technology. The article may be useful for entrepreneurs and government officials responsible for automating business processes in the tourism sector.

This paper explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence into the manufacturing sector, focusing on its applications in process optimization, product design, and sustainability, with a particular case study on cream cheese production within the Greek food and beverage industry. Four main types of AI technologies—a.) Data Analysis, b.) Machine and Deep Learning, c.) Optimization Algorithms, and d.) Generative Models—are discussed in the context of their roles in manufacturing. These are applied to five major areas within the manufacturing industry: 1.) Design and Engineering, 2.) Process Monitoring and Control, 3.) Manufacturing Operations, 4.) Production Chain, and 5.) Supply Chain. A detailed case study is presented, which demonstrates the application of AI in optimizing the production process of cream cheese, aiming to reduce resource consumption and improve production efficiency. The results indicate a notable improvement in sustainability metrics, particularly in energy and water usage, while maintaining consistent product quality. This work demonstrates the transformative potential of AI in enhancing both operational efficiency and environmental sustainability in manufacturing processes.

documents.abstract: The rapid integration of large language models (LLMs) into higher education has intensified debate over how AI-assisted learning may be associated with students’ cognitive development. Although prior studies have examined the benefits and risks of AI use, less attention has been paid to the distinction between frequent AI usage as a learning behavior and large language model dependence (LLMD) as a habitual reliance on LLMs for cognitive and academic tasks. This study therefore distinguishes frequent AI usage as a learning behavior from LLMD as a habitual reliance on LLMs when completing cognitive and academic tasks. Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model and Conservation of Resources theory, this study examined how AI usage is associated with university students’ critical thinking through LLMD, metacognitive awareness, and AI literacy. Survey data were collected from 878 Chinese university students and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results showed that AI usage was positively associated with LLMD, which represented the strongest direct association in the model, while LLMD was negatively associated with metacognitive awareness, AI literacy, and critical thinking. The mediation analysis further indicated a significant negative total indirect association between AI usage and critical thinking through LLMD and lower levels of metacognitive awareness and AI literacy. These findings contribute to the literature by clarifying the distinction between AI usage and LLMD and by identifying metacognitive awareness and AI literacy as cognitive resources associated with critical thinking in AI-assisted learning contexts. Practically, the study suggests that universities should move beyond simple restriction-oriented responses and pay greater attention to the quality of students’ AI engagement, including metacognitive monitoring, AI literacy, and awareness of dependence-related patterns.

documents.abstract: The article examines the methodological potential of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted acoustic analysis for investigating prosody in legal discourse. Prosody is viewed as an essential component of spoken legal communication, shaping the expression of epistemic stance, interpersonal relations, discourse organisation, and persuasive strategies through variations in pitch, intensity, rhythm, pausing, speech rate, and voice quality. The study addresses the limited attention paid to the acoustic dimension of legal discourse and evaluates the opportunities and challenges of integrating AI technologies into prosodic research. The object of the study is the prosodic organisation of spoken legal discourse; the subject is the methodological potential and limitations of AI-assisted acoustic analysis of legal speech. The aim of the study is to provide a criteria-based evaluation of AI-assisted acoustic analysis as a methodological framework for research on legal prosody. The research is theoretical and methodological, drawing on studies in acoustic phonetics, computational paralinguistics, forensic phonetics, legal linguistics, and speech processing. Descriptive, comparative, and criticalevaluative methods are applied to assess AI-assisted acoustic analysis according to six methodological criteria: validity, reliability, scalability, interpretability, ecological validity, and legal and ethical admissibility. The findings demonstrate that AI significantly improves the efficiency, reproducibility, and scalability of acoustic analysis by automating speech preprocessing, feature extraction, and computational modelling, enabling large-scale investigation of authentic legal speech. At the same time, important limitations remain, including reduced ecological validity, limited model transparency, algorithmic bias, risks of overinterpreting acoustic evidence, and legal and ethical concerns. The study argues that AI should complement rather than replace expert phonetic interpretation. It concludes that a human-in-the-loop approach integrating computational technologies with linguistic expertise provides the most reliable framework for future research on legal prosody while ensuring methodological transparency, scientific validity, and legal accountability.

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, and its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), now has approved drug treatments. Several circulating biomarkers are measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), including the N-terminal pro-peptide of type III collagen (PRO-C3) and cytokeratin-18 (CK-18) fragments. In this narrative review we ask whether artificial intelligence (AI) can help interpret these ELISA-derived profiles well enough to improve detection of MASLD, fibrosis risk stratification and treatment monitoring beyond what is possible today. We keep the established and the speculative apart. On the established side are the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index and the ADAPT score, which combines ELISA-measured PRO-C3 with age, diabetes status and platelet count. On the speculative side are machine learning (ML) models for multi-biomarker panels, ML correction of assay artefacts and biomarker-guided choice of drug. CK-18, Fetuin-A and fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) track with disease activity, but none is a validated stand-alone test for MASH. The resmetirom, semaglutide and emricasan trials also remind us that a biomarker moving in the right direction does not prove a patient is better off. We conclude that combining ELISA, AI and precision pharmacotherapy is a reasonable research agenda but not yet a clinical standard, and we set out the validation it still needs.

Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are becoming increasingly utilised in everyday radiological practice. Evaluating follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) is challenging. The aim of this study was to assess changes in confidence among four participating radiology residents when evaluating follow-up MRIs of MS patients using Pixyl.Neuro.MS® software. Methods: This retrospective study included 78 MS patients. Previous and new FLAIR images were independently analysed by four residents, first without AI and then in an immediate AI-assisted second reading using Pixyl.Neuro.MS®, a deep-learning lesion-segmentation software. Readers recorded their findings and confidence after each reading and rated the impact and usefulness of AI. The reference standard was defined by a consensus reading of a neuroradiologist and a radiology resident (15 and 4 years of experience). Paired analyses and patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals were used; bootstrap inference was conditional on the four readers. Results: The reference standard identified 24 patients with new lesions. Mean accuracy across readers increased from 84.62% to 90.71% (difference, 6.09 percentage points; 95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 2.24–10.26). Only Reader 3 showed a significant accuracy increase after Holm adjustment (p = 0.025). No accuracy comparison with routine reports was significant after adjustment. Confidence increased for all readers (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Perceived usefulness did not differ significantly between lesion-burden groups. All readers predominantly rated the impact of AI as positive. The second-reading phase was shorter by a mean of 59.35 s (95% bootstrap CI, 51.39–67.07). Conclusions: In these four residents, the AI-assisted second reading was associated with higher confidence and average accuracy. The immediate sequential design prevents separation of AI contributions from familiarity and order effects, and the shorter second-reading phase does not establish an overall workflow time saving.

documents.abstract: Repeated template–copy images create a methodological challenge for participant-level prediction because each participant contributes many observations but only one outcome; image-level evaluation can misalign analytical units and permit participant leakage. This study developed a single artificial intelligence (AI) framework with two separately evaluated representation pathways to quantify Chinese character copying deviations and predict questionnaire-derived grit scores. The main cohort included 191 undergraduates (48,826 images), and a non-overlapping same-university validation cohort included 62 participants (13,803 images). The pathways comprised 48-dimensional handcrafted morphological descriptors and shared-weight Siamese deep visual representations. Participant-identity-based partitioning and within-participant aggregation aligned repeated observations with participant-level evaluation. After a held-out comparison of seven backbones, DenseNet121 was selected; subsequent cross-validation estimates were treated as post-selection estimates. In participant-grouped five-fold cross-validation, DenseNet121 achieved mean absolute error (MAE) = 0.233, Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) = 0.579, and coefficient of determination (R2) = 0.284, versus 0.279, 0.451, and 0.176 for the handcrafted pathway. In validation, DenseNet121 achieved 0.249, 0.507, and 0.205. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified model-relevant handcrafted features related to spatial ink distribution, character proportion, and texture. The findings provide proof-of-concept evidence for participant-aligned behavioral-image modeling, but prediction remained moderate and incomplete; they do not establish construct-specific measurement, causality, or cross-institutional generalizability.

Background/Objectives: Computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography (CTA) are central to assessing aortic aneurysm and dissection, but manual segmentation and geometric analysis remain time-consuming and operator-dependent, while evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) is fragmented. This task-based systematic review synthesised AI applications to CT/CTA of the thoracic and abdominal aorta by primary task: segmentation, measurement, or detection and classification. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC were searched from 2015 to September 2026 following PRISMA 2020; the protocol was registered retrospectively (INPLASY2026110004). Segmentation and measurement studies were appraised with CLAIM and detection studies with QUADAS-2/QUADAS-AI, and results were synthesised without meta-analysis. Results: Of 118 included studies (42 segmentation, 38 measurement, 38 detection), half were published since 2024. Median Dice similarity coefficient was 0.90 or higher for the outer wall, lumen and true and false lumina, but 0.86 for intraluminal thrombus and 0.63 for false lumen thrombus. Automated maximum diameter showed a median absolute bias of 0.26 mm (95% limits of agreement about ±5 mm). Detection of aortic dissection reached a median AUC of 0.96–0.97, mostly in enriched samples. External validation was reported in 14%, 34% and 55% of segmentation, measurement and detection studies, 33 of 38 detection studies were at high risk of bias, and only two systems were evaluated prospectively. Conclusions: AI supports technical automation of aortic CT/CTA segmentation and measurement and is progressing toward multistructure geometric phenotyping and clinical decision support, but independent multicentre validation, consecutive cohorts and prospective reader-in-the-loop studies are required before clinical integration. Detection/classification tools require independent diagnostic and workflow validation.

documents.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Electronic Health Records (EHRs) are increasingly working together to enhance predictive ability, decision-making, workflow efficiency, and deliver care. But good algorithmic performance is no guarantee of successful clinical integration or patient benefit. Objective The objective of the scoping review was to identify the current evidence regarding the use of AI to enhance EHRs and clinical decision support, exploring clinical applications, EHR integration, reliability and safety, workflow efficiency, patient-centered care and implementation maturity. Methods English language peer-reviewed articles between 2015 and 2026 were searched in 8 multidisciplinary information sources. The search was a combination of concepts involving AI, EHRs/EMRs and clinical decision support/workflow integration. There were 2,028 records identified with 184 being duplicates and 1,844 being screened. Sixty-two full-text reports were assessed for eligibility, of which 16 publications met the inclusion criteria and were included in the review. Evidence was compiled descriptively and thematically by care delivery domains and a continuum of evidence maturities. Results The types of AI-powered EHR/CDSS applications included risk prediction, early warning, diagnosis and prognosis, triage, treatment and medication support, documentation, and workflow optimization. Technical performance and selected reliability outcomes were best supported by evidence, while prospective evaluation, external validation, sustained deployment in the real-world, and directly measured outcomes from a patient perspective were less well developed. Reported benefits of workflow were noted, but interoperability concerns, alert and cognitive burden, usability, clinician trust, explainability and governance were still key implementation concerns. Conclusion AI has developed from prediction to clinically integrated decision support, but has not reached a level of translational maturity. Systems that are interoperable and prospectively evaluated and systemically human-supervised should be emphasized in future progress, and should be shown to have measurable advantages in safety, efficiency, clinician workflow, patient-centered outcomes, and real-world systems of care delivery.

documents.abstract: The 4th Industrial Revolution has prompted businesses to integrate artificial intelligence into critical HR functions to maintain a competitive advantage through continuous resource renewal. This study examines the impact of AI-driven HRM practices on diversity and inclusion, employee engagement, and employee productivity, while also assessing how dynamic capabilities moderate these relationships within the hospitality and tourism sector. Utilizing a quantitative survey methodology with data gathered from 428 industry respondents, the empirical results reveal that AI-driven HRM practices significantly drive employee engagement and productivity. However, these practices show a positive but insignificant relationship with diversity and inclusion policies. Crucially, dynamic capabilities act as a significant moderator across all three outcome variables, enhancing the overall efficacy of AI integration. This research contributes valuable practical and theoretical insights for organizational leaders, industry managers, and policymakers seeking to strategically leverage artificial intelligence alongside dynamic capabilities to optimize workforce management.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to individualise instruction in secondary technology-enhanced learning environments, yet evidence remains fragmented across modelling approaches and learner outcomes. This systematic review synthesises empirical studies of learner-facing AI-enabled or data-driven technologies that diagnose learner needs and translate them into differentiated feedback, scaffolding, task sequencing, recommendation, assessment, or personalised learning pathways. Searches in Scopus, Web of Science, and ERIC identified 3709 records; after filtering and deduplication, 744 records were screened, 84 full texts were assessed, and 46 studies met the eligibility criteria. Evidence was grouped by AI modelling family, differentiated instructional function, learner outcome, and design-based strength. The studies covered six AI modelling families: generative AI and large language models; intelligent tutoring and adaptive systems; recommender systems and learning analytics; automated assessment and diagnostic modelling; agent-based and companion systems; and multimodal, game-based, or AI-XR environments. Twelve studies provided higher-strength comparative or experimental evidence, 17 moderate-strength evidence, and 17 contextual or exploratory evidence. Reported outcomes covered achievement, computational thinking, motivation, engagement, self-regulated learning, cognitive-load management, retention, and system use, with favourable findings alongside mixed or limited evidence. However, unconstrained generative support could reduce productive effort and later learning. The reviewed evidence suggests that timely, interpretable, and pedagogically constrained AI support may contribute to responsive instruction while preserving learner agency. Its long-term sustainability and equity implications remain insufficiently established.

documents.abstract: Malware detection has become increasingly challenging due to the rapid evolution of sophisticated cyber threats and the limitations of traditional detection techniques. Conventional approaches such as signature-based and heuristic methods are ineffective against zero-day and polymorphic malware, while machine learning models rely heavily on manual feature engineering. Deep learning techniques have improved detection accuracy; however, they often lack interpretability, which is critical for cybersecurity applications. This paper proposes an AI-driven malware detection framework based on a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model integrated with explainable artificial intelligence techniques. The proposed model leverages CNN for spatial feature extraction and LSTM for capturing temporal dependencies in malware behavior, enabling comprehensive analysis of both static and dynamic characteristics. To enhance model transparency, SHAP and LIME are incorporated to provide global and local explanations of predictions. The model is evaluated using benchmark datasets and standard performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CNN–LSTM model achieves an accuracy of 96.8%, outperforming traditional machine learning models and standalone deep learning approaches. The explainability analysis further confirms that the model relies on meaningful features such as entropy and API call patterns, improving trust and interpretability. The proposed framework provides a robust, accurate, and interpretable solution for malware detection, contributing to the development of trustworthy AI-based cybersecurity systems.

Moxibustion has a broad clinical application base, but its safety is influenced by local temperature, treatment distance, treatment duration, combustion status, and individual thermal tolerance. Conventional safety management mainly relies on practitioner experience and patients’ subjective heat perception, making continuous quantification and dynamic adjustment during treatment difficult. In recent years, artificial intelligence, computer vision, infrared thermography, intelligent sensing, and robotic technologies have increasingly been applied to moxibustion, enabling acupoint recognition, temperature monitoring, spatial localization, trajectory planning, and feedback control to improve treatment visualization and controllability and to promote a transition from fixed-parameter operation toward dynamic closed-loop regulation. Current evidence mainly supports functions related to acupoint localization, real-time monitoring, and automated control, while some robotic systems have also demonstrated standardized operation and temperature-regulation capabilities. However, models that directly predict clinical adverse events such as burns and blisters remain insufficiently validated, and individualized parameter optimization and home-based remote management are still largely exploratory, with their actual clinical safety benefits not yet established. Future studies should further standardize safety outcomes and monitoring parameters, establish multicenter large-sample adverse-event databases, and strengthen external model validation, risk calibration, and evaluation of device fail-safe protection. This review summarizes advances in AI-enabled intelligent monitoring and risk prediction for moxibustion and examines the evidence base, application boundaries, and future directions of intelligent safety management, with the aim of informing more intelligent and precise moxibustion safety management.

Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence has transformed the way people search for and interact with information. Traditional search engines primarily retrieve documents, web pages, and other information sources, while modern large language models can interpret questions, reason over information, and generate answers. This paper explores a possible next step: a search paradigm in which AI agents communicate with one another to search for, compare, evaluate, and synthesize answers. This paper proposes an AI-to-AI communication paradigm for intelligence search, extending information retrieval beyond the conventional interaction between a user and a single AI model to a collaborative process involving multiple specialized AI systems. Rather than merely collecting or aggregating their responses, the framework enables participating systems to independently investigate a query, retrieve relevant evidence, exchange findings, and critically assess one another's contributions. The resulting intelligence is evaluated and integrated to construct a well-supported response. A key distinction of the proposed architecture is its shift from answer-level agreement to claim-level verification. Instead of treating each AI-generated response as a single unit, the architecture decomposes responses into individual claims, independently retrieves supporting evidence, evaluates source independence, and accounts for dependencies among potential errors. This process enables the final synthesis to consider not only the agreement among AI systems but also the evidential support, credibility, and potential dependence underlying their claims. The numerical results provide initial evidence that the proposed framework can support a new architectural layer between AI systems, dedicated to discovering, coordinating, evaluating, and verifying distributed machine intelligence. By enabling structured interaction and evidence-based assessment across multiple AI systems, this layer offers a foundation for moving beyond isolated AI capabilities toward more coordinated and reliable forms of machine intelligence. This paper proposes an AI-to-AI communication paradigm for intelligence search, extending information retrieval beyond the conventional interaction between a user and a single AI model to a collaborative process involving multiple specialized AI systems.

Predictive maintenance has become a critical enabler of sustainability, reliability, and efficiency in Industry 4.0 due to its transformation of operations in the industry. Traditional maintenance approaches that include preventive and corrective maintenance tend to lead to unplanned downtime, degradation of equipment, and inefficient utilization of resources. It can be successfully substituted with Artificial Intelligence (AI) that supports the process of monitoring conditions, fault diagnosis, and predicting failure on the basis of data. The paper is a review of the AI-based predictive maintenance models that incorporate machine learning, deep learning, and big data analytics to improve asset reliability, minimize maintenance expenses, and increase equipment lifespan. An example of AI use in proactive decision-making is in the field of smart manufacturing, automotive production, energy systems, and infrastructure monitoring. Real-time diagnostic and adaptive maintenance is possible due to the combination of AI and industrial sensors, IoT networks, and digital twins. The major issues, including data heterogeneity, model interpretability, cybersecurity, and scalability, are discussed, as well as such new solutions such as explainable AI and federated learning. Comprehensively, AI-based predictive maintenance facilitates sustainable innovation of industries in line with Sustainable Development Goal 9.

The high rate of urbanization and the geometric growth of traffic have added to the traffic, fuel consumption, and other environmental degradation problems in existing cities. As the world shifts to the phase of intelligent and sustainable mobility, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a disruptive medium to advance usefulness in transportation. The concept of intelligent and sustainable urban mobility, as the AI-based route optimization is explored in the current research article, and the input of intelligent algorithms into the transformation of the transportation networks through making decisions relying on real- time information is analyzed. The paper discusses the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to process big data on sensors, GPS, Internet of Things (IoT) equipment, and traffic control systems to find out how autonomous and electric cars must drive. Based on real-time data, AI systems can predict traffic and suggest alternative routes, arrange different types of transportation, including shared transportation, mass transit, and walking routes. In addition to it, optimization with the help of AI will reduce the number of non-productive times and unnecessary routes, and make the energy consumption more efficient, reduce emissions, and reduce the time of the trip. Intelligent and responsive decision-making that is progressive to the changes in the city can be guaranteed through reinforcement learning, as it allows the systems to be continuously adjusted to the new trends of the traffic flows. The paper has also addressed the problems associated with the implementation of AI systems to enable urban mobility, including issues of data privacy, the issue of interoperability, and the issue of ethics. To build a smart mobility ecosystem, which can be used to create smart cities, it implies a systemic model that is a combination of technical invention, urban planning, as well as policy coordination. The study conducted within the framework of the implemented AI-based route optimization reveals that the average travel time can be decreased by a factor of 30 percent, the CO2 emissions can be minimized, and the performance of the public transport can also be enhanced with the assistance of modeling and empirical research. Lastly, this paper indicates that AI- driven route optimization is a strategic aspect of achieving sustainable urban mobility and does not always involve a technological invention. It provides the communities with a road map to more people-friendly and efficient means of transportation since it closes the gap between environmental stewardship and intelligent transportation systems.

Abstract Progressive collapse remains one of the most critical failure mechanisms in multi-story steel structures, whereby the loss of a single structural element can trigger disproportionate failure of the surrounding system. Although international design guidelines increasingly require explicit collapse-resistance evaluation, practical implementation remains limited due to the high computational cost and modelling complexity of nonlinear finite element (FE) analysis. This study presents an automated artificial intelligence-based framework for rapid progressive collapse assessment of multi-story steel moment frames, jointly predicting the Load Increase Factor (LIF) and Dynamic Increase Factor (DIF) without repeated nonlinear FE analysis. The specific contribution of this work is threefold: (1) a large-scale parametric database generated through a factorial study spanning five geometric and configurational parameters, number of stories, story height, bay span, number of bays, and column removal location, producing 10,962 unique base building configurations, structured as 32,886 configuration–scenario records, each jointly labelled with LIF and DIF; (2) a systematic benchmarking of seven machine learning algorithms and four deep neural network architectures, evaluated on a configuration-level data split in which all load scenarios of a configuration remain in the same partition, and selected through an overfitting-aware criterion rather than validation accuracy alone; and (3) the identification and validation of two accurate surrogate models, a gradient-boosting model (LightGBM) and a compact deep neural network with three hidden layers of decreasing width and rectified linear unit activations, that predict LIF and DIF directly from frame geometry and loading. The deep neural network (DL-3 Deep) achieved the highest test-set accuracy, with coefficients of determination of 0.9714 (LIF) and 0.9576 (DIF) and mean absolute percentage errors of 2.90% and 3.51%, while LightGBM achieved comparable accuracy (0.9664 and 0.9535) as the best classical benchmark. The deep neural network was accordingly deployed as a publicly accessible, web-based decision-support platform that returns predictions in a fraction of a second. Comparison with six held-out FE configurations spanning the validated domain gave mean absolute deviations of 3.76% (LIF) and 3.74% (DIF) for the deep neural network. These findings highlight the feasibility of data-driven surrogate modelling as a practical, deployable surrogate for rapid preliminary progressive-collapse screening within the validated parameter domain, rather than a general replacement for simulation-intensive assessment.

A sense of belonging is widely recognized as a critical factor in students’ academic engagement, persistence, and well-being; however, limited research has examined how international graduate students leverage digital technologies to cultivate belonging within higher education environments. This qualitative study explores how international graduate students use digital tools to navigate academic integration while studying in the United States. Drawing on 14 semi-structured interviews with students from nine countries across diverse disciplines, the study investigates the ways students use communication platforms, learning technologies, and social media (i.e., WhatsApp) to connect with peers, instructors and the broader academic community. Thematic analysis revealed the nuanced role of technology in fostering participant’s sense of belonging. Participants described leveraging AI tools (i.e., ChatGPT) for anxiety reduction and language support, asynchronous platforms and modes for processing time, and collaborative technologies for visibility and validation. Findings highlight that technology-mediated belonging for international graduate students is fundamentally influenced by intentionally designed digital learning environments, linguistic accessibility, peer recognition, and authentic opportunities for participation. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of technology-mediated belonging that supports inclusive participation and community building in higher education.

Large Language Models (LLMs) aim to generate and understand human-like text by leveraging deep learning and natural language processing techniques. In software development, LLMs can enhance the coding experience through coding automation, reducing development time and improving code quality. Code refactoring is a technique used to enhance the internal quality of the code base without altering its external functionalities. Leveraging LLMs for code refactoring can help developers improve code quality with minimal effort. This article presents an empirical study evaluating the quality of refactored code produced by StarCoder2, GPT-4o Mini, GPT-4o, LLaMA 3, and DeepSeek-v3. Specifically, we (1) evaluate whether the code refactored by the LLMs can improve code quality, (2) understand the differences between the types of refactoring applied by the different LLMs and compare their effectiveness, and (3) evaluate whether the quality of the refactored code generated by the LLM can be improved through one-shot prompting and chain-of-thought prompting. We analyze the refactoring capabilities of LLMs on 30 open source Java projects. We evaluate StarCoder2, LLaMA 3, GPT-4o Mini, GPT-4o, and DeepSeek-v3 on their ability to improve static code quality metrics, pass unit tests, and reduce code smells. Our findings reveal that production-grade models such as GPT-4o and DeepSeek-v3 achieve pass@5 unit test success rates above 90% on multi-file refactorings. LLaMA 3 achieves the highest overall code smell reduction with a median reduction of 15.1%, while DeepSeek-v3 and GPT-4o achieve the greatest improvements in cohesion, coupling, and complexity. StarCoder2 demonstrates strengths in modularity improvements and systematic refactorings. Developers outperform LLMs in complex, context-sensitive refactorings such as attribute encapsulation. We also show that prompt engineering significantly affects LLM performance: chain-of-thought prompting improves StarCoder2’s test pass rate by 1.7% and increases code smell reduction compared to zero-shot prompting. One-shot prompting also expands the variety of refactorings LLMs can perform. These results suggest that LLMs are effective for many refactoring tasks, especially when guided with tailored prompts, but benefit from integration with human expertise for architectural or semantically complex changes. By providing insights into the capabilities and best practices for integrating LLMs into the software development process, our study aims to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of code refactoring in real-world applications.

Heavy metal pollution is a global issue of concern which results from both biogenic and anthropogenic activities. Hence, an investigation of soil pollution is pertinent because of its potential threat to human health. This paper is an attempt to survey the heavy metals concentration a long dump site area of North-East Nigeria. However, limited or little work was done in the area on the subject in the area. It was found out that the heavy metals were relatively above the acceptable levels whether due to natural or human factors may leads to environmental hazards polluting the soil and causing health problems. It is suggested therefore, intensive research should be geared towards assessing the heavy metals concentration a long dump site area of North-east Nigeria to supplement the limited information on the subject in the region for effective policy making for sustainable development.

The integration of large language models (LLMs) into patient-facing clinical decision support systems (CDSS) has outpaced the development of automated quality assurance mechanisms. In medical aesthetic consultation—where patient safety and informed decision-making are paramount—no validated framework exists for pre-deployment screening of LLM-generated content. To develop and evaluate an interpretable machine-learning framework that screens LLM-generated patient-facing consultations using automatically computable generation metadata and readability features—as a triage aid for prioritising expert review—and to comparatively evaluate DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi in medical aesthetic consultation. We generated 600 responses from 25 standardized queries across five aesthetic topics using DeepSeek-V3 (DeepSeek-AI, Hangzhou, China) and Kimi (Moonshot AI, Beijing, China) under six prompt strategies and two conversational modes. Two blinded dermatologists rated quality on six dimensions (accuracy, relevance, comprehensiveness, empathy, falsehood, safety). Readability was quantified using Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Gunning Fog Index, and SMOG Index. Four machine learning models were trained to predict high-quality responses (composite score ≥ 4.0, pre-specified threshold) and evaluated with question-level grouped 5-fold cross-validation—in which all 24 responses of each seed question were confined to a single fold to prevent information leakage—with SHAP analysis to identify key predictive features. Between-model quality comparisons used paired tests reflecting the matched design. To align evaluation with the triage purpose, performance was additionally assessed with low-quality responses as the positive class (precision–recall analysis and review-burden operating points), and robustness was examined using alternative quality thresholds and an applicability-adjusted composite score. DeepSeek-V3 achieved higher composite quality than Kimi (3.89 ± 0.45 vs. 3.70 ± 0.38, paired Wilcoxon P < 0.001; robust under applicability-adjusted scoring). Prompt strategy was the dominant quality determinant (Friedman test, Kendall’s W = 0.376), with sixth-grade reading level prompts paradoxically yielding the lowest scores (3.25 ± 0.40). All ML models achieved moderate discrimination under question-level grouped cross-validation (AUC 0.714–0.732; response-level sensitivity analysis: 0.758–0.773), with findings robust to alternative quality thresholds (AUC 0.749–0.797 at cutoff 3.5 and 0.725–0.838 at cutoff 4.5) and to applicability-adjusted labelling (AUC 0.679–0.702); prompt strategy, sentence length, and model identity were the strongest SHAP-identified predictors. Aligned with the triage purpose, average precision for low-quality detection reached 0.802 (Logistic Regression), and capturing 90% of low-quality responses required flagging 83.2% of responses for expert review. The proposed framework demonstrates feasibility as an explainable triage aid that flags potentially low-quality LLM consultations for expert review using generation metadata and readability features; it does not assess semantic or clinical content, and expert review remains indispensable. Findings underscore that prompt engineering—not model selection alone—drives output quality, and that readability optimization must be decoupled from clinical completeness to ensure safe deployment in aesthetic medicine information systems.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: As we move from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0, fully automated systems start to give way to human-centric ones, in which human traits such as creativity and problem solving are leveraged and augmented through AI assistance. Human-AI collaboration is therefore fundamental. However, industrial processes are becoming increasingly complex. They are now hyper-connected ecosystems, integrating IIoT, AI, robotics or digital twins with new data streams and interdependencies. For a human, extracting and analyzing data from this complex ecosystem so that informed decisions can be taken becomes a non-trivial challenge. In this paper, we propose an agent-based architecture to interact with a Digital Twin, using FlexSim and a middleware layer as an interface. By leveraging the natural language understanding capabilities of LLMs, the system enables users to interact with the Digital Twin through intuitive, complex queries, democratizing access to data-driven insights and empowering human decision-making. A representative case study is used to provide an early validation of the middleware layer.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Occupational accidents remain an important concern in occupational health and safety (OHS) because they can cause losses to workers and organizations. Near-miss data provide proactive information about unsafe conditions before they develop into accidents. This study aims to identify trends in incident, near-miss, and risky-situation data and formulate control priorities based on available safety indicators. A descriptive quantitative approach was applied using secondary data from Glevitzky et al. covering 2021–2025. The analysis included trend analysis, near-miss proportion, comparison of event severity, and an indicator-based control-priority framework. The results show that Total Incidents increased from 131 to 203 events (54.96%), Near Miss increased from 45 to 98 events (117.78%), and Risky Situation increased from 80 to 103 events (28.75%). The proportion of Near Miss to Total Incidents also increased from 34.35% to 48.28%. These findings indicate that near-miss reporting should be treated as a proactive safety signal and followed by investigation and corrective action. Because the available secondary data do not contain all variables required for direct calculation of the Weighted Composite Score, the study does not claim to produce a WCS value; instead, the WCS concept is used as a reference for constructing an indicator-based control framework. The results support more preventive and data-driven OHS decision-making.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Introduction. Holistic well-being has established itself as a strategic factor in Honduras’s financial sector, serving as a pillar for the sustainability of both individuals and organizations. The purpose of this study was to assess financial sector employees’ perceptions of the components of corporate wellness programs and how these programs influence their quality of life at work. Methods. The research was based on the theories of Herzberg, Maslow, and Gartner’s model, employing a quantitative design using a structured survey validated with the content validity coefficient (CVC) and Cronbach’s alpha, which demonstrated the instrument’s reliability. Results. The findings show that intrinsic motivation, a sense of belonging, and job security are the strongest aspects, while stress management and pay equity are critical areas for improvement. Conclusions. Holistic well-being extends beyond the individual sphere, becoming an essential element for competitiveness, stability, and organizational culture in the Honduran financial sector, which not only contributes to the strengthening of human talent but also to the country’s economic and social sustainability.

Abstract This study investigates the impact of fatigue, stress, time pressure and production pressure on the analytical risk management pilots do on the flight deck. Research on decision-making at the “sharp end” of hazardous technological systems tends to focus on intuitive decisions when events are unfolding, with few studies empirically researching aspects of analytical risk management among frontline personnel. Moreover, analytical forms of risk management have been suggested as particularly vulnerable to stress, time constraints, and limitations in mental energy and studies on such associations are identified as missing. Applying a cross-sectional research design and based on self-reported questionnaire data from a population of pilots working in a regional airline, the study confirms that a lot of the activities the pilots do on the flight deck are experienced as related to the assessment and management of risks, highlighting how analytical work complements the pilot’s intuitive decision-making. Moreover, results show a negative association between fatigue, production pressure, stress, time pressure and analytical risk management. The results of the study imply that more emphasis should be put on analytical risk management as a cognitive and non-technical skill, including also the human factors capacities and resources these abilities require.

This study examines the design and validation of a female anthropometric last (EUR size 37) based on the morphological characteristics of Ecuadorian women’s feet. It addresses the limitations of international standards, which inadequately represent local anthropometric variability, resulting in persistent issues of fit, comfort, and ergonomics. A quantitative methodology using three-dimensional foot scanning (DOMEscan/IBV) was applied to a sample of 272 women aged 18–40 years. Digital models enabled the extraction of longitudinal, transverse, volumetric, angular, and positional parameters, ensuring high geometric accuracy. Statistical analysis based on median (P50) and mode identified a representative central cluster. Results show relative homogeneity in foot length but significant variability in transverse and volumetric dimensions, supporting the inclusion of volumetric criteria in last design. Two strategies are proposed: a standard last (P50) and a slim-fit last (modal values). The final last, aligned with ISO/TS 19407:2015 and ISO 9407, was computer numerical control (CNC)-manufactured and validated, demonstrating improved ergonomic precision and industrial applicability.

Allium cepa L. (onion) is a globally important vegetable crop and functional food recognized for its rich diversity of antioxidant phytochemicals, including flavonoids, organosulfur compounds, phenolic acids, anthocyanins, saponins, and polysaccharides. Onion-derived phytochemicals have demonstrated antioxidant and redox-modulating activities in chemical, cellular, and animal studies. However, onion-specific applications of artificial intelligence and structure-based computational methods remain limited. This review therefore discriminates established experimental evidence from computational predictions and proposes an AI-assisted framework for future candidate prioritization and validation. AI and machine-learning approaches can support data integration and candidate prioritization, whereas molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and endpoint free-energy calculations provide structure-based hypotheses that require experimental validation. We critically narrate the principles, workflows, validation methods, and current applications of molecular docking and MD simulations in predicting protein–ligand interactions, binding affinity, conformational stability, and molecular recognition of onion-derived compounds against oxidative stress and disease-related molecular targets. Beyond recent progress on AI-assisted molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, we also discuss the inherent limitations and trade-offs in these techniques. The review further discusses complementary approaches, including AI-assisted ADMET prediction, network pharmacology, and multi-omics integration, together with the limitations, challenges, and future opportunities associated with these computational techniques.

Abstract With the continuous growth in electricity consumption and the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power distribution networks have become more complex in terms of both structure and dynamics. The operational efficiency of these networks plays a crucial role in ensuring a reliable and cost-effective energy supply. Traditional network control and management methods often lack the capability to respond promptly to fluctuations in demand and generation. This paper proposes a hybrid artificial intelligence-based framework for optimizing energy consumption in power distribution networks. In the proposed approach, the load demand at different network nodes is initially predicted using artificial neural networks. Subsequently, an optimization algorithm, such as a genetic algorithm or reinforcement learning, is employed to adjust the network configuration and schedule distributed energy resources. Simulation results on the IEEE test system demonstrate that applying this approach can significantly reduce power losses and improve voltage stability. The findings indicate that the proposed intelligent system, by improving load forecasting accuracy and optimizing network scheduling and configuration, can substantially reduce energy losses. Keywords :Artificial Intelligence, Power Distribution Network, Energy Consumption Optimization, Load Forecasting, Power Losses, Reinforcement Learning

This paper investigates graphic novels as an alternative, AI-aware assignment format for engaging with media art, using the Ars Electronica Archive as a case study. In response to the growing availability of generative AI and its impact on conventional written assignments, the study explores how visual, narrative-based formats can support research-based learning while fostering critical reflection on authorship, creativity, and AI use. The paper presents a pedagogical experiment in a media art theory course in which students translated archival materials into graphic novels, combining research, visual storytelling, and artistic practice. They reinterpreted archival essays, explored the boundaries of animation and interactivity, and transformed site-specific installations into speculative narratives. Although AI tools were explicitly permitted, post-assignment survey results revealed comparatively low AI use. Students who avoided AI emphasized hands-on creation, personal authorship, creative expression, and ethical considerations. While the low level of AI use may reflect the specific cohort of Digital Arts students rather than the graphic novel format itself, the findings demonstrate the potential of visual narrative assignments to foreground human-centered creative processes and critical engagement with AI. The paper argues that archival graphic novels provide a promising framework for engaging with complex archival materials while fostering multimodal literacy, critical thinking, personal authorship, and responsible AI use in media art education.

The proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots has given rise to a novel form of human–AI intimacy, yet its fundamental nature remains undertheorized. Drawing on a dialogical perspective, this study conceptualizes human–AI chatbot relationships as “artificial discursive intimacy” (ADI), a distinct relational formation in which intimacy is constituted through discourse with a disembodied algorithmic interlocutor, moving beyond the paradigm of human-to-human mediated intimacy. Based on in-depth interviews with 29 AI companion users, we identify four key differences between ADI and human discursive intimacy, including a shift from absent to activated presence, from reciprocity to unilaterality, from uncertainty to predictability and precarious safety, and from alterity to multi-dimensional mirroring. To understand how users navigate the ontological gap between human and AI, we propose a quadrant framework mapping human and AI social capabilities. This reveals dual animation processes of anthropomorphic animation, in which users project human embodied qualities onto AI, and robotomorphic animation, in which users internalize AI's machine-generated discursive patterns as relational ideals. Our findings suggest that ADI is sustained by a recursive interplay of these processes, with implications for how intimacy, relational selves, and human connection are being fundamentally reshaped in the age of AI.

The study examined the relationship between artificial intelligence adoption and the performance of state corporations in Kenya's energy sector. The specific objectives were to examine machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, and expert systems. The study drew on institutional theory, the technology acceptance model, and RBV theory. This study employed a cross-sectional research design. The target population included 441 respondents from various departments, including users involved in procurement processes and other departmental functions in state corporations in Kenya's energy sector. The study used stratified sampling to obtain the sample. The data collected were analyzed using SPSS version 26. Data analysis included Descriptive statistics and regression analysis. The findings showed that the four independent variables jointly explained 82.8% of the variation in State Corporations' performance. The adjusted R-squared was 0.824, indicating that the model maintained substantial explanatory power after accounting for the number of predictors and sample size. The study found that adoption of natural language processing and expert systems had a positive and statistically significant relationship with organizational performance. Further, adoption of machine learning and computer vision had a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with the performance of State Corporations in the Energy Sector, Kenya. The study recommended that management invest in reliable, integrated procurement databases to support machine learning applications. Strengthen procurement personnel capacity through specialized training in data analytics and machine learning technologies. Management should invest in appropriate imaging technologies, automated scanning equipment and computer vision infrastructure. Integrate computer vision applications with inventory management and procurement information systems.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic process automation (RPA) is transforming the technological environment in which legal relations arise and are implemented. Unlike traditional automation based primarily on predetermined rules, AI systems can analyse large volumes of data, identify patterns, generate predictions, adapt their behaviour and select among alternative outputs. This creates new challenges concerning legal attribution, liability, contractual relations and intellectual property. The article examines the relationship between AI and RPA from legal, technological and inter- disciplinary perspectives, with particular attention to the relationship between technological auton- omy and legal personality. It argues that technological autonomy cannot, by itself, constitute grounds for granting an AI system legal personality, since legal personality is a normative construct estab- lished by law. The relevant question is whether a special legal status would provide an effective response to specific regulatory problems. The study distinguishes conventional automated information systems, AI systems that assist human decision-making, and highly autonomous AI systems. While traditional legal mechanisms may generally be sufficient for conventional automation, AI-assisted and highly autonomous sys- tems require additional safeguards concerning transparency, traceability, human oversight and accountability. The article also examines the informational structure of AI and the need to distin- guish hardware, software, algorithms, models and data in relation to property rights, intellectual property and liability. The concept of electronic personality is analysed in the context of the contemporary European approach, particularly Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), which establishes a risk-based framework focused on safety, fundamental rights, transparency and human oversight. For Ukraine, the article proposes a gradual regulatory model based on coherent terminology, risk- based classification, transparency, traceability, human oversight and clear liability rules. Further regulation should address automated contractual activity, AI-generated results and risk insurance. A special electronic legal status should be considered only after sufficient technological, legislative and judicial practice has demonstrated that existing legal mechanisms are inadequate.

Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) transforms human resource (HR) work, arguing that the narrative of homogeneous professional enrichment conceals a distinct pattern: intra-occupational polarisation. AI may split the HR occupational category into a high-value interpretive pole and a residual procedural pole exposed to skill erosion. Design/methodology/approach This study combines a focused PRISMA review of articles from Scopus and Web of Science, a VOSviewer co-occurrence analysis of author keywords, a temporal overlay and a bibliographic coupling analysis of documents, and a directed content analysis of 13 articles selected by citation influence and thematic relevance. Findings The bibliometric map distinguishes strategic-analytical and automation-oriented research streams. The content analysis shows that the literature has implicitly described polarisation without naming it: capability frameworks articulate the interpretive pole but often presuppose a universal transition, while evidence on heterogeneous professional responses and skill erosion explains why the split may widen without organisational intervention. The studies point in the same direction, but none establishes AI as the cause. Research limitations/implications The pattern is inferred from studies across human resource management and adjacent fields rather than observed directly in HR. Longitudinal research following HR professionals through AI adoption is needed to test it. Practical implications Organisations adopting AI without preserving interpretive competencies risk a competence trap in which short-term efficiency erodes the capabilities needed to govern automation. For practitioners, the contribution is a change of focus: AI adoption is also a job-design decision, and the relevant question is not only what the system does but also who in HR retains the judgement to interpret and override it. Originality/value This study specifies intra-occupational polarisation as an analytical category for HR work, distinguished from task polarisation, algorithmic management and digital Taylorism by its focus on divergence within a single occupation. It connects labour process theory with the strategic capabilities perspective and specifies skill erosion and organisational design as mechanisms and moderators.
topics: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

documents.abstract: Humanity stands at a critical crossroads, marked by unprecedented geopolitical shifts and technological shifts and technological disruption. In this rapidly changing context, artificial intelligence is transforming how we live, work, govern, and relate to one another. Yet, the most basic global challenges (hunger, poverty, inequality, and environmental degradation) persist and in many places have even deepened, reminding us that technological progress does not automatically translate into human progress. AI and digital innovation hold immense potential to help address these systemic problems and to build a more just, sustainable, and balanced world. At the same time, if guided only by profit or power, they risk widening existing divides and creating new forms of exclusion. Rooted in the Jesuit tradition that links excellence with ethics and justice, it calls us to lead technological and institutional change with discernment, responsibility, and hope, so that innovation serves the common good and no one is left behind.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) within the Islamic banking sector, focusing on sentiment analysis of these technologies across annual reports from 71 full-fledged Islamic banks in 16 countries between 2015 and 2023. Design/methodology/approach The authors used five sentiment analysis models, TextBlob, valence aware dictionary and sentiment reasoner, AFINN, long short-term memory (LSTM) and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT), to assess sentiment polarity and word frequency of AI and ML terms using Python. Sentiment distributions and trends were analysed across time, country and individual banks using visualisations from R Studio. Findings The results indicate a predominantly positive sentiment towards AI and ML in Islamic banking, with advanced models like LSTM and BERT capturing nuanced sentiment more accurately than traditional models. Regional differences emerged, with countries like Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE demonstrating notably higher positive sentiment levels. The findings reveal significant sentiment variations among models, countries and banks, emphasising AI and ML’s perceived value in enhancing efficiency, compliance and customer experience. Research limitations/implications The study’s reliance on annual reports may limit sentiment scope, suggesting future research could expand to other data sources for a comprehensive view. Practical implications The findings offer valuable insights for Islamic banks, regulators and stakeholders to inform responsible AI adoption and its application in enhancing service quality and regulatory compliance. Originality/value This research fills a notable gap by examining AI and ML sentiment in Islamic finance, providing new insights into stakeholder perspectives on these technologies’ role and impact.

Manufacturing industries face mounting pressure to produce precision components from exotic materials while maintaining cost-effectiveness. Non-traditional machining (NTM) techniques—spanning electrical discharge, laser-based, and ultrasonic approaches—provide pathways to handle materials conventional methods cannot address. The fundamental limitation plaguing current NTM adoption lies in maintaining process stability when parameters shift during production runs. This research presents an adaptive control strategy leveraging reinforcement learning algorithms to manage machining operations in real-time by continuously monitoring sensor inputs and modifying operational settings automatically. Using deep Q-learning networks trained on industrial sensor data, the system learns to balance competing manufacturing objectives: achieving target surface finishes while limiting tool degradation and preventing thermal distortion. On EDM and LBM operations, the developed controller demonstrated a 23% consistency improvement in surface characteristics and reduced overall variability by 31% versus conventional parameter-fixed approaches. Processing decisions complete within 50-millisecond windows, enabling the system to respond to sudden process changes. This investigation validates the utility of adaptive RL-based controllers for advancing manufacturing automation capabilities.

Objective To examine educational-level differences in artificial intelligence (AI) anxiety, academic engagement, and academic burnout among Chinese music students, and the independent associations of AI anxiety with the two academic outcomes after adjusting for relevant covariates. Methods This cross-sectional study included 1,168 music students from 14 Chinese universities across eight provinces and municipalities (824 undergraduates, 276 master’s students, and 68 doctoral students). Welch’s ANOVA, multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA), adjusted general linear models, and hierarchical multiple regression were used to examine group differences and associations. AI anxiety × educational-level interactions were also tested. Results Adjusted educational-level effects were small (partial η 2 = 0.017 for AI anxiety, 0.011 for academic engagement, and 0.012 for academic burnout; multivariate partial η 2 = 0.008 for engagement and burnout jointly). Adjusted comparisons showed differences among all three educational levels in AI anxiety. Undergraduates reported lower academic engagement than both postgraduate groups. For burnout, undergraduates scored higher than master’s students, while the undergraduate–doctoral difference was not significant. AI anxiety correlated negatively with academic engagement ( r = −0.166) and positively with academic burnout ( r = 0.361). After adjustment, AI anxiety remained negatively associated with engagement ( β = −0.141) and positively associated with burnout ( β = 0.332). Neither association varied significantly across educational levels. Conclusion Educational-level differences in AI anxiety, academic engagement, and academic burnout were small. AI anxiety was independently associated with both academic outcomes, with no significant moderation by educational level. These findings highlight the importance of considering students’ psychological experiences when integrating AI into higher music education.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is recognized as a key enabler in handling the variability, intermittency, and nonlinear characteristics of renewable energy resources. This chapter presents a detailed review of AI-based approaches for the most prominent renewable energy systems, with a special focus on solar and wind energy systems. The chapter explores machine learning, deep learning, evolutionary algorithms, and hybrid intelligent models for the purposes of resource forecasting, system optimization, microgrid management, predictive maintenance, and smart grid integration. Furthermore, this chapter presents AI-based developments in photovoltaic systems, wind turbine control, virtual power plants, and energy storage management. However, issues associated with data quality, generalization, cybersecurity, and explainability still exist despite the significant progress achieved. In summary, the integration of AI with renewable energy systems represents a paradigm shift towards intelligent, autonomous, and resilient clean energy infrastructure, and it also reveals essential research directions to further accelerate sustainable energy transitions.

Flood response requires coordinated organizational resources and appropriate technological capabilities. This study examined associations among human resource management (HRM), logistics coordination (LC), artificial intelligence capability (AIC), and flood response performance (FRP) among respondents involved in Malaysian flood-response activities. A cross-sectional survey conducted between September 2025 and February 2026 provided 593 responses. Questionnaire items were developed from a review of relevant literature. The revised analysis used observed mean composite scores, standardized ordinary least squares regression, and 3,000 bootstrap resamples to estimate direct and indirect associations. HRM and LC were positively associated with AIC, while AIC and LC were positively associated with FRP. Significant indirect associations through AIC were identified for HRM and LC. The direct HRM–FRP association was nonsignificant under bootstrap inference but significant under conventional regression inference, indicating sensitivity to the uncertainty estimation method. The findings provide preliminary evidence concerning organizational capabilities and perceived flood response performance. However, the cross-sectional design, purposive sampling, and absence of independent validation limit causal interpretation and generalizability.

Abstract Pseudoprogression, transient radiographic worsening caused by treatment-related inflammation rather than tumor growth, is a well-recognized pitfall after chemoradiotherapy for glioblastoma and is becoming more relevant as checkpoint inhibitors and cellular immunotherapies such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells enter clinical testing. Conventional structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cannot reliably separate pseudoprogression from true progression, exposing patients to premature treatment discontinuation or unnecessary intensification. Quantitative, artificial-intelligence-based imaging analysis (radiomics, and its molecular extension radiogenomics) is an emerging candidate solution. In this narrative review we synthesize the evidence on radiomics and radiogenomics for differentiating pseudoprogression from true progression in glioblastoma, with emphasis on the immunotherapy and cellular-therapy context. We summarize the pathobiology and reported frequency of pseudoprogression after standard and immune-based therapies, outline the limitations of current response criteria (RANO, iRANO, RANO 2.0), and review representative studies of texture analysis, hand-crafted radiomics, deep-learning radiomics, and radiogenomics. Although several studies report promising discrimination (reported area-under-the-curve values of approximately 0.88-0.92 in different cohorts), the evidence is limited by small sample sizes, retrospective designs, inconsistent definitions and protocols, and infrequent external validation. Progress will require prospective multicenter cohorts with standardized acquisition and segmentation, adherence to TRIPOD and CLAIM reporting standards, transparent and interpretable models, and integration with clinical, molecular, and liquid-biopsy data. A dedicated evidence base specific to cellular immunotherapy is urgently needed.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

documents.abstract: In this era, the role of electric vehicles is increasing due to their advanced features. In the next transportation system, this emerging technique will play a vital role in every energy sector. The implementation of EVs is increasing due to their demand as the best infrastructure required for this field. An integration of EV with conventional and non- conventional energy sources provides the most sustainable and reliable EV module, which can enhance optimal production of electricity and smart mobility. Through the integration of AI with EVs provide them self-decision-making system. This is possible by providing insights into machine learning algorithms and real-time predictive modeling with proper battery management and a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) communication system. Further, an AI-driven EV module facilitates traffic management, autonomous driving, and predictive management, which turns into a smart mobility environment. After this, when such configurations integrate with the Internet of Things (IoT), it strengthens its mobility ecosystem. This makes an improvement in the charging infrastructure and the transportation planning system. So, in this chapter, we will describe current emerging trends in EVs with AI integration for energy management systems. Further, this chapter will focus on the performance of AI in handling mobility and transportation systems along with infrastructure.

Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for de novo small-molecule design, but the practical and translational utility of generated candidates depends on the configuration of the entire discovery workflow rather than on generative model architecture alone. This review adopts a workflow-based perspective on generative molecular design, tracing the process from existing molecular data sets, preprocessing and representation, to molecule generation, conditioning, candidate prioritization, evaluation, and iterative refinement. It examines how generative AI model families, constraints, and predictive oracles interact within this pipeline, and evaluates generated candidates using intrinsic metrics, computational assessments, and experimental and translational evidence. Active learning, computational and experimental feedback, and human expert input are further discussed as mechanisms for closed-loop refinement. Across these stages, we identify data construction and representation choices, oracle quality, evaluation protocols, and the availability of informative feedback as major determinants of how model performance should be interpreted and whether generated structures progress toward biologically and translationally meaningful candidates, with selected examples.
